title: Stability Orchestra: Cross-functional Pilot & SLO Campaign (June 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc lays out a 12-week cross-functional pilot to validate a repeatable program for improving service dependability via well-scoped Service Level Commitments (SLCs) and SLOs, improved observability signals, and rapid remediation playbooks. We intentionally use an "orchestra" metaphor: each team (strings/performance, brass/autoscale, percussion/ops-runbooks) rehearses their piece, then we run full-rehearsal (failure injection + canary) and a public performance (gradual rollout).

Goals (outcomes):
- Define and validate SLC/SLO bundles for three representative services (edge-gen, prompt-router, embedding-index).
- Bring down mean time to detect (MTTD) for high-severity availability incidents from ~9m to <=3m in pilot services.
- Demonstrate automated error-budget-aware routing to trigger fallback variants under load and keep user-visible errors <0.5%.
- Produce a cross-team runbook template and a lightweight SLO adoption checklist to scale beyond pilot.

Scope (what's in/out):
In scope:
- SLO definition, alert thresholds, ownership handoff for the three pilot services.
- Instrumentation gaps: tracing, prefix cache hit metrics, token-level latency distribution (p50/p95/p99).
- Small-scale chaos experiments and canary policy tests in staging and a limited production ring.
Out of scope:
- Full org-wide SLO rollout, pricing/cost model changes, long-lived infra refactorings outside pilot servicing layers.

Roles & Responsibilities (conductor model):
- Conductor (Pilot lead): Avery Chen — coordinates cadence, cross-team decisions, stakeholder comms.
- Strings (performance): Jordan Patel — kernel selection, batching profile changes, p95 tuning.
- Brass (autoscale & infra): Samir Desai — burst pool configs, scale policies, pod draining playbook.
- Woodwinds (observability): María González — dashboards, alert mappings, tracing instrumentation.
- Percussion (ops & runbooks): Lina Park — oncall playbooks, incident postmortems, runbook templates.
- Customer success liaison: Ethan Brooks — identifies customer-facing impact windows and communications.

Conductor Cadence (meetings):
- Weekly sync (30m): tactical status, blockers, next actions.
- Biweekly demo (45m): service-level dashboards, canary results, runbook rehearsals.
- Engineering stakeholder review (every 4 weeks): decision gates for rollout and scale.

12-week timeline (high-level):
- Week 0 (planning): finalize pilot services, owners, success metrics, create JIRA epic REL-2026.
- Weeks 1–2 (instrument): add missing metrics (prefix cache hit, kv-cache warm start, token-latency histograms); baseline measurements.
- Weeks 3–4 (SLC/SLO workshops): draft SLOs, error-budget policies, alert thresholds; stakeholder sign-off.
- Weeks 5–6 (runbooks & rehearsals): author playbooks, runbook drills in staging, create automated alert-to-runbook links.
- Weeks 7–8 (sectional pilots): run targeted experiments (batching tweaks, cache priming, autoscale stress).
- Weeks 9–10 (chaos + canary): introduce controlled failures (network partitions, GPU OOM), execute canary rollout in limited prod ring.
- Weeks 11–12 (evaluation & handoff): collect metrics, retro, finalize SLO adoption checklist and rollout playbook.

Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
- Quantitative: pilot services meet target SLOs for 7-day window with error-budget burn <= 10% during canary.
- Observability: required dashboards show live p50/p95/p99 and error budget burn-rate charts; alert-to-runbook links exist.
- Operational: runbook drills completed with median MTTD <=3m and MTTR <=20m across drills.
- Handoff: product and platform teams accept the SLO artifacts and runbook templates.

Experiment matrix (examples):
- Cache Warmup Pilot: measure response improvement when prefix cache is pre-warmed for top-10 prompts. Metrics: cache-hit-rate, p95 latency.
- Batch Aggression Test: increase batching window by 10–30ms during off-peak and observe cost/latency tradeoffs. Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, throughput tail.
- Fallback Variant Routing: route overflow traffic to lower-cost quantized variant when error budget burn exceeds threshold. Metrics: user error rate, cost delta.
- Autoscale Drain Safety: simulate pod termination while streaming responses; verify graceful fallback and no user-visible truncations.

Runbook excerpt (template lines):
- Symptom: sudden spike p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10m + error-rate > 0.5%.
- Immediate check: look at recent deploys (last 15m), prefix-cache hit-rate, GPU/memory contended nodes.
- Quick remediation: switch traffic to previous model revision, trigger scale-out policy, enable fallback routing.
- Post incident: collect traces, mark incident in JIRA REL-2101, schedule 48h postmortem.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: instrumentation gaps produce blind spots. Mitigation: schedule dedicated instrumentation sprint and block any SLO sign-off until key metrics exist.
- Risk: canary causes customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: very narrow production ring (1%) + rollback automation + CS communication draft pre-approved.
- Risk: error-budget automation misfires and routes traffic prematurely. Mitigation: add simulated dry-run phase and manual approval gate for the first two activations.

Communications plan:
- Internal: weekly pilot digest (email + slack #reliability) and biweekly demo recordings.
- Exec: 6-week checkpoint via short slide deck (one slide per pilot service: baseline, change, result).
- Customers: CS to prepare templated messaging for planned canary windows and immediate rollback play.

Acceptance & Handoff artifacts:
- Final SLO bundle per service (documented SLC, SLO, alerting thresholds, owner).
- Observability dashboard templates (Grafana links) and alert definitions (Prometheus/Alertmanager).
- Runbook template and drill report (dates, participants, MTTD/MTTR).
- Playbook to replicate pilot in new service (step-by-step checklist).

Next steps (first 10 days):
1) Kickoff meeting: confirm owners, finalize REL-2026 epic and child tickets (assignee per task).
2) Instrumentation sprint: Woodwinds allocate 2 engineers for metric gaps (target 10 days).
3) Runbook skeleton: Percussion drafts initial template and schedules first drill in staging.
4) Canary ring config: Brass sketches production ring and rollback automation.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What availability target should we standardize on for internal pilot services (99.5% vs 99.9%)?
- How aggressive should automated fallback be vs requiring manual approval on first activations?
- Is there appetite to include cost-budget guardrails as part of the SLO bundle in pilot?

Appendix: quick metrics to track during pilot
- p50/p95/p99 latency (token-level)
- Error-rate (user-visible 4xx/5xx)
- Error budget remaining and burn-rate (1h, 24h windows)
- Cache hit-rate (prefix & KV caches)
- Autoscale events per hour, scale latency

Contact & versioning:
- Pilot lead: Avery Chen (avery.chen@redwood.ai)
- Doc version: 0.3 (in_review)
- Last modified: 2026-06-28 by Avery Chen

Notes: This doc is intentionally pragmatic and workshop-oriented — expect frequent edits after early instrumentation runs. Use the linked artifacts for tickets and experiment logs.
